extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners who appear before the USPTO (particularly those subject to Office of Enrollment and Discipline matters), OED staff, and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Formal USPTO disciplinary order implementing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when an attorney has been suspended by a state authority; describes procedural steps, grounds for discipline, and post-discipline notifications/obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State when that authority suspends an attorney from the practice of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Order imposes suspension of Respondent from practice before the USPTO for one year, predicated upon the Indiana Supreme Court's suspension. The Office acts pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service requirements for § 11.24 proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' must be sent to the Respondent (e.g., by certified mail) and published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order in this matter was sent by certified mail (receipt numbers provided) to multiple addresses and published in the Official Gazette for two consecutive weeks; evidencing adequate service for the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's opportunity to respond and default consequence (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case Respondent did not file a response; accordingly, the Office determined under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) that no genuine issue of material fact exists and suspension is the appropriate discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent representation (Indiana Professional Conduct Rule 1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney must provide competent representation; failure to do so is a basis for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Indiana Supreme Court found Respondent failed to provide competent representation, a predicate for suspension in the reciprocal proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable fees (Indiana Professional Conduct Rule 1.5(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney must not make an agreement for, charge, or collect an unreasonable fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Indiana order cited Respondent for making an agreement for, charging, or collecting an unreasonable fee — conduct forming part of the basis for suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision and use of nonlawyer assistants (Indiana Rule 5.3 / Guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney is responsible for use/supervision of nonlawyer legal assistants and must not employ or rely upon unsupervised nonlawyers in a manner that undermines the lawyer's role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Indiana order found Respondent used a nonlawyer legal assistant who was not an employee and shared fees with an unsupervised paralegal in a manner that made the attorney's role secondary to the paralegal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper fee sharing with nonlawyers (Guideline / Rule 5.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney must not improperly share legal fees with a nonlawyer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Indiana order cited improper sharing of legal fees with a nonlawyer as one of the violations supporting suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (Indiana Rule 8.4(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney must not engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the Indiana order include harassment of a client about a grievance, inducing others to harass, filing frivolous claims against opposing counsel, and submitting false affidavits — conduct characterized as prejudicial to the administration of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney must avoid conflicts of interest, including representing adverse interests in the same matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Indiana order identified a 'blatant conflict of interest' where Respondent appeared on behalf of both the party seeking support and the party resisting support — a specific example of impermissible conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candor and truthfulness to tribunals and in filings
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney must not make false statements to a trial court or submit false affidavits or other false evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Indiana order found Respondent made false statements to the trial court and attached an affidavit to a tort-claim notice that he later acknowledged was false; such dishonesty was part of the disciplinary findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on frivolous or abusive filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing frivolous claims or instruments for an improper purpose is sanctionable conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Indiana order cited Respondent's filing of a frivolous Notice of Tort Claim against the Commission's counsel as an example of sanctionable abusive conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of misconduct admissions and stipulations in sanctioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions under oath and stipulations by a respondent that adjudicate misconduct may be used in determining sanctions, though respondents may still challenge findings on review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order notes Respondent admitted under oath the truth of the allegations and joined in a request to be heard on sanctions alone, but later filed a petition for review challenging the hearing officer's finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition and scope of USPTO discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may suspend a practitioner's ability to practice trademark and non-patent law before the USPTO for a specified period as reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Final Order suspends Respondent from practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for one (1) year, effective the date of the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-discipline compliance obligations (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disciplined practitioner must comply with post-discipline obligations set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs Respondent to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (the Order does not restate § 11.58's contents but mandates compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification of discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of public discipline and the reasons for it to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts where the respondent is admitted, and to the public pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order instructs the OED Director to publish a notice materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Suspension' in the Official Gazette and to notify relevant agencies and courts as required.
